rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a physical crack or opening, especially one made by breaking or parting.

example.english: The cup broke, and there's a gap on the edge.
example.traditional: 個杯跌爛咗，邊位有條罅。
example.jyutping: go3 bui1 dit3 laan6 zo2 bin1 wai2 jau5 tiu4 laa3

rows.note: Use this for a free period or open slot in a schedule rather than a physical opening.

example.english: I have a gap at three this afternoon, so I can see you.
example.traditional: 我下晝三點有個空檔，可以見你。
example.jyutping: ngo5 haa6 zau3 saam1 dim2 jau5 go3 hung1 dong2 ho2 ji5 gin3 nei5

rows.note: Use this for a shortfall or missing amount, such as a staffing or funding gap.

example.english: This project is still short by three hundred thousand; the funding gap is quite big.
example.traditional: 呢個計劃仲爭三十萬，個資金缺口幾大。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 zung6 zaang1 saam1 sap6 maan6 go3 zi1 gam1 kyut3 hau2 gei2 daai6

rows.note: Use this for an unfilled vacancy or vacant post, rather than a general shortfall.

example.english: The company still has several vacant posts, so the staffing gap needs filling urgently.
example.traditional: 公司仲有幾個空缺，個人手空缺要盡快填補。
example.jyutping: gung1 si1 zung6 jau5 gei2 go3 hung1 kyut3 go3 jan4 sau2 hung1 kyut3 jiu3 zeon6 faai3 tin4 bou2
